Hi Priya  thanks for the worksheet and diagram, really helpful. Short answers inline + proposed plan: 

On your questions:
1) Offline installer: Yes  we provide an air-gapped installer bundle (signed artifacts + checksums) that can be loaded via encrypted media. Installer validates signatures locally; no outbound calls required.
2) Offline upgrade: We support two modes:
   - Rolling upgrade (preferred): requires at least one staging host so we can drain traffic and migrate KV caches; minimizes downtime but needs extra capacity during upgrade window.
   - Full-window upgrade: can upgrade in-place but requires full downtime for the inference cluster for the duration of the window.
3) Fallbacks: we recommend a staged snapshot + pre-flight checks; our recommended recovery is rolling back to last known-good image on the staging host, then redeploying. We’ll provide a runbook for the pre-flight validations.

Hardware guidance (high level):
- Minimum pilot: 2x A100-class GPUs (or equivalent) + 4 CPU hosts for control plane; 12TB NVMe per GPU for model cache.
- Production: typical starting point is 48 GPUs depending on concurrency; we’ll finalize after you share load estimates.

Next steps:
- Rishi (ccd) will run a short technical walkthrough and map the installer/upgrade flow to your maintenance window.
- Can you share a preferred slot for week of Dec 14? We’ll prepare an offline upgrade runbook and a checklist tailored to your change control.

Attaching updated redwood_onprem_requirements_v1.pdf with brief notes.

Hi Priya / IT team 

Im Rishi, Solutions Engineer at Redwood  Ill run the technical session. A few clarifications and recommendations after reviewing your worksheet: 

1) Installer and artifacts:
- We deliver a signed tarball plus a checksums file and GPG signature. The tarball includes an installer binary and all model artifacts necessary for the pinned model variants.
- For very large model sets we split artifacts across multiple encrypted drives.

2) Upgrade pattern and maintenance window mapping:
- For your 4-hour monthly window we recommend a rolling upgrade with a single staging host. Typical flow: pull artifacts to staging via secure transfer -> run pre-flight checks (disk, network, checksum) -> drain one node -> promote staging -> verify metrics -> drain next node. We can complete a non-major patch in ~6090 minutes per node in our lab; real-world times vary.

3) Hardware specifics (pilot recommendation):
- GPUs: 2x NVIDIA A100 40GB (or equivalent Ampere-class).
- CPU: 32 vCPUs per inference host.
- RAM: 512GB per GPU host recommended for larger context models.
- Disk: 2TB NVMe per host for model cache + 1TB for OS/logs.
- Network: 25GbE internal; management plane can run on isolated 1Gb interface.

4) KV cache persistence and rollback:
- We persist KV cache to local NVMe and snapshot to the staging host before an upgrade. If a rollback is required we restore snapshots from staging; this typically avoids a full cold-start.

5) HSM/KMS integration:
- We can integrate with your HSM for sealing keys; the installer will accept an HSM provisioning bundle and an admin key for initial bootstrap.
